{{nihongo|'''Hazu Shrine'''|幡頭神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Miyazaki, Kira-chō, {{ill|Nishio|Q317844|qid=Q317844}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking}} it was classified as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. {{nihongo|'''Hazu Shrine'''|幡頭神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mikawa Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* {{ill|Takeinadane|Q11486691|qid=Q11486691}}
* {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake no Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Ōmononushi|lt=Ōmononushi|Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}}

The principal deity is {{ill|Takeinadane|Q11486691|qid=Q11486691}}, who is said to have been the {{ill|Owari no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11465294|qid=Q11465294}} and, according to tradition, served as “Hatagashira” (banner commander) during {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru}}’s eastern expedition. {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake no Mikoto}} and {{ill|Ōmononushi|lt=Ōmononushi|Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} are also enshrined together.

== History ==
It is traditionally said that the shrine buildings were established in Taihō 2 (702)<ref name="nishio" />. According to legend, the enshrined deity Takeinadane no Mikoto died at sea off Izu while returning from the eastern campaign with Prince Yamato Takeru, and his body drifted ashore at the coast of Miyazaki, where local villagers enshrined him<ref>[https://www.japan-net.ne.jp/~kira-spa/sightseeing_spot/01-10.html Hazu Shrine - Mikawa Bay Quasi-National Park, Kira Miyazaki Coast, Kira Onsen] Retrieved December 5, 2018</ref><ref name="nishio" />.

In the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}, compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 (927), the shrine appears as “Hazu Shrine” in {{ill|Mikawa Province|Q768158|qid=Q768158|lt=Mikawa}} {{ill|Hazu District|Q522936|qid=Q522936}}, and is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}{{Sfn|Hazu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. It is also recorded in the *Mikawa Province Register of Deities* as “Senior First Rank Haridai Myōjin, seated in Hazu District”{{Sfn|Hazu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}.

The present main hall was rebuilt in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō}} 8 (1580)<ref name="nishio" />.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji}} 4 (1871), under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}}, it became a village shrine, and in {{ill|1921|Q2162|qid=Q2162}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174|lt=Taishō}} 10) it was promoted to a prefectural shrine. On April 30, 1921 (Taishō 10), the main hall was designated a Specially Protected Building under the then {{ill|Ancient Temples and Shrines Preservation Law|Q11411552|qid=Q11411552}}<ref>Ministry of Education Notification No. 352, April 30, Taishō 10 (see: [{{NDLDC|2954737}} National Diet Library Digital Collections])</ref>. After the enforcement of the {{ill|Cultural Properties Protection Law|Q1188502|qid=Q1188502}} on August 29, {{ill|1950|Q18597|qid=Q18597}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 25), it became designated as an {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}. == Grounds ==
[[File:Hazu shrine2.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main hall (National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}})}}{{small|Kumano Shrine and Shinmei Shrine on the left and right.}}]]
The shrine grounds are situated on a hill overlooking {{ill|Mikawa Bay|ar|خليج ميكاوا|be|Мікава (заліў)|ceb|Mikawa-wan (luuk sa Hapon, lat 34,75, long 137,08)|de|Mikawa-Bucht|eu|Mikawa Badia|fa|خلیج میکاوا|fr|Baie de Mikawa|he|מפרץ מיקאווה|ja|三河湾|ko|미카와만|no|Mikawabukta|pl|Mikawa (zatoka)|pt|Baía de Mikawa|ru|Микава (залив)|th|อ่าวมิกาวะ|tr|Mikawa Körfezi|zh|三河灣|qid=Q1154346}}. The three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} main hall with a cypress bark roof dates from Tenshō 8 (1580). Though small in scale, its decorative motifs employ robust curved lines, and the interior carvings and *kamaboko* (strut) forms are simple in style. The roof is covered with cypress bark, and the deeply curved eaves are a distinctive feature<ref name="nishio">[https://www.city.nishio.aichi.jp/index.cfm/8,14703,91,408,html Cultural Properties of Nishio City: Hazu Shrine Main Hall - Nishio City] Retrieved December 5, 2018</ref>.

In addition to the main hall, the grounds include a worship hall, side hall, sacred horse shelter, purification pavilion, and shrine office. There are also subordinate shrines: Shinmei Shrine and Kumano Shrine.

File:Hazu-jinja (Nishio), Shinmei-sha.jpg|Shinmei Shrine (National Important Cultural Property)
File:Hazu-jinja (Nishio), Kumano-sha.jpg|Kumano Shrine (National Important Cultural Property)
</gallery>

== Cultural properties ==
== Important Cultural Properties (National designation) ==
* Hazu Shrine, 3 structures (buildings) – The main hall was designated on April 30, Taishō 10 (1921)<ref>{{National Cultural Properties Database|102|1278|Hazu Shrine Main Hall}}</ref>, and on September 20, Reiwa 4 (2022), the main halls of the subordinate Kumano Shrine and Shinmei Shrine were additionally designated<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 121, September 20, Reiwa 4.</ref>.
** Main hall (with 3 attached ridge tags) – constructed in Tenshō 8 (1580).
** Subordinate Kumano Shrine main hall (with 4 attached ridge tags) – constructed in Tenshō 8 (1580).
** Subordinate Shinmei Shrine main hall (with 4 attached ridge tags) – constructed in Tenshō 8 (1580).
The subordinate Kumano Shrine main hall and Shinmei Shrine main hall had previously been designated as Tangible Cultural Properties of Aichi Prefecture in Shōwa 32 (1957).
